title: Questions About Crowdfunding for a Quantitative Trading Product (HFT-Focused)
author: PressureScary2400

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: Three months live and still can't cover server costs means the alpha isn't big enough to scale. Raising money just buys you more time to lose, fix the edge first.

replies.author: PressureScary2400
replies.body:
Thank you, that is a really good question.  
The truth is, server and GPU costs are extremely expensive. Maybe you haven’t worked directly in AI or quantitative research, so it’s difficult to appreciate the scale of the costs involved.

There’s a reason hedge funds and ETFs exist. If someone could consistently achieve an edge of over 30% per month, they could simply raise capital from their own family and close circle.

I’m also building everything from scratch on my own, so all I can do is manage risk, continuously improve my models, and research more optimal approaches. That’s why I need to raise capital.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: an investor's first question will be why three months of live alpha can't pay for its own servers. and raising outside money to trade it usually means securities lawyers before any platform, worth pricing that in.

replies.author: PressureScary2400
replies.body:
Thank for your opinion.  
Actually, the fundraising is to invest in dedicated servers, not to increase trading capital. Owning and maintaining servers for research and running models also comes with significant costs.

I don’t think any self-funded fund could fully cover all these expenses after just three months, especially when you factor in research costs.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: fair, servers aren't trading capital. but backers handing over money for something that trades will expect a share of what it makes, and that's what turns it into a security, whatever the money buys. and at three months in, renting compute by the hour usually beats owning boxes.

replies.author: PressureScary2400
replies.body:
Yeah, you're right. But there are so many architectures to experiment with and so much data to share that I can't afford to rent 5–6 servers simultaneously, especially when the data sources are so large and include images, text, chunks, and more.

I'm trying to find ways to optimize costs, but bandwidth and GPU expenses account for the largest share of my research budget.

Thanks so much for your input. Your perspective is very practical and grounded in reality.

replies.author: TheGratitudeBot
replies.body: Thanks for saying that! Gratitude makes the world go round

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: for research boxes, spot or preemptible instances run a fraction of on-demand and you only pay while an experiment runs. keep the raw images and text in object storage in one region and pull just the slice each run needs, moving data inside a region is usually free or close to it.
